moduleTitle: Generating coded test steps with CLI actions in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Describe the documented Copilot assistance for supported coded steps, including CLI validation.
Describe the difference between a CLI action and a Custom action in Testim.

elements.description: CLI actions/validations execute Node.js in the connected CLI environment; browser custom actions execute in the browser. Node.js can use configured packages and authorized resources, but network access, credentials and dependencies still need setup.

elements.text: Browser DOM access and Node.js resource access are different capabilities. Browser/API checks can also validate server-provided results; direct database-driver access is the scenario-specific CLI use case, not a ban on all browser-based backend assertions.

bulletPoints: CLI actions/validations = custom Node.js scripts run in the CLI environment, not the browser.
Direct database-driver checks can use a configured CLI environment; runtime alone does not guarantee connectivity.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Copilot assistance for supported coded steps

elements.term: Generate a draft, then insert and test it
elements.description: The Coding Assistant documentation explicitly lists Add CLI Validation among supported steps. Open Write code with AI, acknowledge the notice and request code. Use Paste code at cursor or Copy code to insert it; appearing in chat does not automatically install the implementation.

elements.text: The original Academy CLI-action recording was unavailable. This local guide uses the explicitly listed CLI validation path rather than certifying every action variant. Review runtime, parameters, package bindings and returned Promises before relying on the generated draft.

bulletPoints: Copilot’s documented supported list includes CLI validation.
Request a draft, insert it deliberately and validate runtime/setup and behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to validate a database value from a regular custom (browser) action
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Writing a browser-context custom action that attempts to open a direct database connection.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For direct database-driver queries, configure a CLI step with the required package, credentials and network access. Browser/API outcome assertions are distinct supported approaches.

examPitfalls.title: Treating generated chat code as an installed implementation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming requesting code automatically applies and validates it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use a documented supported step, insert the draft explicitly, review and test it. Configure required packages/parameters and return asynchronous completion as required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What environment do CLI actions and validations execute in?

options.text: Inside the browser's JavaScript sandbox, same as a regular custom action.
As custom Node.js scripts executed in the CLI environment.
On a remote Testim-managed cloud function with no local access.
Inside the AUT's own backend server process.

practiceQuiz.rationale: CLI actions and validations are custom Node.js scripts executed in your CLI environment, initiated from inside a test like a standard custom action — but running outside the browser, unlike regular custom actions.

optionExplanations.A: Browser custom steps use a different runtime.
optionExplanations.B: CLI steps execute Node.js in the CLI environment.
optionExplanations.C: The runtime is not universally a managed cloud function with no local access.
optionExplanations.D: The step does not execute inside the AUT backend process by default.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test must query a database through its Node.js driver in an authorized connected runtime. Which listed step fits this direct query?

options.text: A regular custom validation running in the browser.
A CLI validation with the configured database driver, credentials and network access.
This isn't possible in Testim at all.

practiceQuiz.hint: Direct driver access requires the configured runtime, not merely selecting a step type.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The CLI runtime can use the required Node.js driver with configured access. This does not prohibit browser/API checks of server-provided results; those are different from the stated direct query.

optionExplanations.A: A browser step does not load the stated direct Node.js database driver.
optionExplanations.B: The configured CLI validation can perform the authorized driver query.
optionExplanations.C: Visible checks do not query the database driver.
optionExplanations.D: Configured CLI database checks are supported.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can Copilot assist a documented supported CLI validation step?

options.text: It cannot assist CLI validation steps.
Generate a code draft from a description, then insert, review and test it in the configured CLI runtime.
Copilot converts the CLI action into a browser-based custom action automatically.
Copilot can only explain existing CLI action code, never generate new code.

practiceQuiz.hint: Generated code in chat still needs deliberate insertion and validation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented supported list includes CLI validation. Generate offers a draft; insertion, package/parameter setup and behavior testing remain required.

optionExplanations.A: The supported list explicitly includes CLI validation.
optionExplanations.B: A draft is generated, then deliberately inserted and validated.
optionExplanations.C: Assistance does not automatically convert the execution runtime.
optionExplanations.D: Generate can propose code, not only explain existing code.

quickRecap.value: Custom Node.js script run in the CLI environment, initiated from inside a test.
Configured Node.js packages and resource access support direct database and file checks; access is not automatic.
Documented CLI validation assistance produces a draft; insert, review and test it.
